name: devops-networking
description: Use when configuring or debugging Linux server and infrastructure networking - host firewall with nftables (iptables-nft, ufw, firewalld as front-ends), bridges/bonds/VLANs with netplan, ifupdown2, systemd-networkd or NetworkManager, static and policy routing, DNS (systemd-resolved, Unbound/BIND/CoreDNS, split-horizon), TLS and ACME certificates (certbot, acme.sh, lego, HTTP-01 vs DNS-01), reverse proxies (Traefik, Nginx, Caddy, HAProxy), WireGuard (and Tailscale/Headscale as a pointer) and layer-by-layer network troubleshooting. Not for Kubernetes networking, Gateway API or CNI (devops-kubernetes, devops-k8s-cluster), Docker networks (devops-docker), Proxmox SDN (devops-proxmox), Neutron (devops-openstack), or security audit and TLS grading (fuse-security:security-headers, security-expert).

findings.excerpt: ip -br a ; ip r ; ip rule                     # state
| ifupdown2 (`/etc/network/interfaces`) | `ifquery -a -c` is NOT a safe check; read the diff | no built-in timer: `cp interfaces interfaces.bak` then `systemd-r
| `rm -rf /etc/letsencrypt` / deleting `acme.json` | Loses the account key and issued certificates; re-issuing counts against CA rate limits | Back up first |
